claims.statement: EMA's Clinical Trials Information System publicly exposes trial details including therapeutic area, sponsor, recruitment dates, and a map that helps patients and clinicians locate recruiting trials.
The EU Clinical Trials Regulation uses a common system for multinational applications while emphasizing participant safety, transparency, and protection of personal data.

contrary_evidence: CTIS already makes trials discoverable, so a simple trial-search interface is not differentiated.
Laboratory values alone may be insufficient for accurate eligibility screening.

economics.acquisition_route: Choose one lab-heavy therapeutic area, obtain ethics and privacy review, then contract a paid sponsor pilot and a single lab site; no patient contact occurs without explicit consent.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 2500 enrollments yearly at 3500 PLN net revenue yield 8.75m PLN annual revenue; at 30% EBITDA, 4x EBITDA, and 55% founder ownership, equity is about 5.8m PLN in year 6-9, with retained earnings counted only inside equity.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: 12-18 hours weekly, with privacy, ethics, and clinical operations specialists contracted against pilot revenue.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 55-70% after laboratory share, privacy operations, and manual eligibility QA.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 30000-70000 PLN per sponsor-and-lab launch, recovered after 12-25 enrolled participants depending on the fee.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 200-500 PLN per consented verified pre-screen or 3000-8000 PLN per enrolled participant, with 20-35% shared with the lab.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Revenue repeats across trials and sites rather than as a patient subscription; sponsors renew only if enrollment quality is demonstrated.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Structured eligibility rules, referral outcomes, and site-specific screen-failure reasons improve matching operations
fingerprint.customer: Consenting diagnostic-lab customers who may qualify for recruiting clinical trials
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Laboratory chains place the opt-in inside result portals repeatedly used by tested patients
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Consent-gated local matching and referral infrastructure with outcome-based recruitment fees
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Sponsor or CRO pays per verified pre-screen or enrolled participant, with a contracted share to the laboratory
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A trial opens with eligibility criteria that include recent laboratory or demographic fields

founder_fit: Connects the founder's data-science, neuroscience, genetics, and health interests.
Rule-based pre-screening can be built before attempting regulated predictive models.
Lab distribution supplies repeated patient access without influencer marketing or cold patient outreach.
risks: Consent, ethics, and health-data governance errors would be severe.
Biased matching could worsen representation or create inappropriate expectations.
Sponsor sales cycles and trial starts are irregular.

structure.control_point: Consent and eligibility translation layer between lab result delivery and trial sites
structure.critical_dependency: Ethically approved lab participation and sponsor willingness to pay for attributable enrollment

thesis: Allow diagnostic labs to offer an explicit opt-in when a customer retrieves results. A locally executed rules engine checks only consented fields against publicly recruiting trial criteria, and sends a structured pre-screen to a site only after separate contact consent. Trial sponsors or CROs pay for verified pre-screens or enrollment and share revenue with the lab; the product never sells a patient list or exposes non-consenting records.
title: Consent-First Trial Match Rail for Lab Networks
uncertainties: Whether Polish labs and ethics bodies accept a commercial opt-in referral workflow.
Which therapeutic areas have lab-heavy criteria and costly recruitment gaps.
How sponsors define and verify a billable pre-screen or enrollment event.
